title: Goldman Sachs expects Bank of England to raise rates again in February
description: Goldman Sachs has revised its outlook on the Bank of England's interest rates, now predicting a possible quarter-point rise in November's monetary policy meeting. This would be the first increase since 2023, influenced by climbing energy costs and robust economic growth. Although immediate policy shifts are unlikely, the Bank will vigilantly observe inflation risks, maintaining rates at 4.25% through mid-next year.

title: Missed Reliance Industries’ historic 8% one-day rally? Here’s what technical analysts are saying
description: Reliance Industries shares surged on Monday, marking their sharpest single-day rally in nearly seven years and adding Rs 1 lakh crore to its market capitalisation, taking it to Rs 17 lakh crore. The rally followed strong Q2 FY27 results, with consolidated net profit rising 41% year-on-year to Rs 25,548 crore and revenue growing 29% to Rs 3.32 lakh crore. The oil-to-chemicals segment led earnings growth, with EBITDA jumping 68% to a record Rs 25,203 crore.

title: South Eastern Coalfields files DRHP with SEBI for IPO; Coal India to offload 66.8 crore shares
description: Coal India subsidiary South Eastern Coalfields has filed its draft papers with SEBI for an IPO comprising an offer for sale of up to 66.81 crore shares. One of India’s largest coal producers, SECL reported higher revenue and profit and plans to list on the BSE and NSE.

title: Office, retail and warehousing offer new opportunities as India’s real estate market matures: JLL
description: India’s commercial real estate market is entering a new phase, with office, retail and warehousing offering fresh opportunities for institutional investors, a JLL report said. Despite cap rates hitting historic lows, the sector continues to offer double-digit unlevered returns over five years. With limited scope for further compression, future returns will increasingly depend on rental income growth and operational efficiencies.

title: Bitcoin rattled by biggest crypto heist in history! Why Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger hated cryptocurrency
description: A reported $6 billion crypto heist at Binance has rattled investors and revived concerns about cryptocurrency risks. Binance said its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which may have enabled unauthorised withdrawals. The FBI blamed North Korea for the attack, while Binance said it would cover the losses.

title: Big tech share buybacks plunge 83% as AI spending hits cash flows
description: Major US technology companies sharply reduced dividends and share buybacks as record AI infrastructure spending pushed their combined free cash flow into deficit. The shift raises concerns about shareholder returns and places greater pressure on Big Tech to deliver profit growth from its AI investments.

title: Explained: Why gold investors should tone down expectations as yellow metal plunges to a 1-year low
description: Gold has fallen more than 30% from its January record high, with rising oil prices, inflation concerns and expectations of further Fed rate hikes adding to pressure. Analysts remain cautious about a near-term recovery, even as major banks retain bullish forecasts for 2027.

title: Nasdaq Outlook: Is the worst over for AI-fuelled tech stocks?
description: Wall Street’s AI-led rally faced a sharp setback as the Nasdaq recorded its biggest single-day fall since June. Heavy losses in technology stocks reflected growing investor concerns over hyperscaler spending and the returns on artificial intelligence investments.

title: Coal India shares jump 4% after firm records highest-ever monthly coal supplies in October
description: Coal India shares jumped more than 4% after the state-run miner reported record monthly coal production and supplies in October. Total supplies crossed 70 million tonnes for the first time, while deliveries to the power sector reached an all-time high of 57.1 million tonnes.

title: Pizza Hut, KFC India operator's Q2 loss naarrows sharply on strong same-store sales growth
description: Devyani International, the parent company of KFC and Pizza Hut in India, has recorded a significant reduction in losses during its second quarter. For the third straight quarter, same-store sales for KFC increased by 4.4%. With revenues climbing by 10.4% to 15.19 billion rupees and expenses only rising 8.3%, Chairman Ravi Jaipuria emphasized the ongoing challenges posed by inflation and increasing interest rates.
